case_title: Velthepu Srinivas and Others v. State of Andhra Pradesh (Now State of Telangana) and Anr.
accused_victim_relationship: Accused and victim from the same village and same family group (as stated in the judgment); alleged political rivalry and animosity after a Gram Panchayat election in which the victim's sister won and the wife of one accused (A-4) lost.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302 read with s.34 (for A-3 altered to IPC s.304 Part II)
weapon: Axe, sword, stone and knife (a stick was also seized as material object)
evidence_type: Eyewitness testimony (PWs 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8); medical (post-mortem by PW-11); recovery of weapons and lungi on accused's pointing; Section 164 CrPC statements; forensic report; photographs and sketch of scene
confession: Confessional statement recorded by PW-18 leading to recovery of axe, sword and knife; the judgment does not expressly rely on it for the decision
aggravating_circumstances: Multiple sharp-weapon injuries (12 injuries, 10 by sharp weapons); fatal injury at back of neck by axe; victim dragged from auto-rickshaw and attacked by several accused
mitigating_circumstances: For A-3 only: did not wield the axe, used only a stone, some witnesses said he merely threatened them, no common intention found
trial_court_outcome: All four convicted under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 500 each, default one month simple imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Initial acquittal of all accused (21.06.2007) was set aside by the Supreme Court and remanded; on remand the High Court confirmed the conviction and sentence and dismissed the appeals (26.04.2022)
offence_finally_established: A-1, A-2 and A-4: murder under IPC s.302 r/w s.34. A-3: culpable homicide not amounting to murder under IPC s.304 Part II
neutral_facts: The victim was travelling to a nearby town in an auto-rickshaw on a morning in November 2001, with two co-passengers. The accused are four men from the same village and family group as the victim. Earlier, a relative of the victim had won a village council election against the wife of one accused, and the resulting rivalry between the two groups is alleged to be the motive. When the auto-rickshaw reached a house belonging to one accused, one accused stopped the vehicle and pulled the victim out by his legs. Another accused joined in and dragged him toward that house. The accused are alleged to have attacked him with an axe, a sword, a stone and a knife. The victim's son, an eyewitness, reported the matter to the police the same evening. The investigating officer found the body in the front yard of the house, took photographs, prepared a sketch, and conducted an inquest in the presence of panch witnesses. The post-mortem recorded twelve injuries, ten caused by sharp-edged weapons, including a partial amputation of three fingers of the left hand and a deep lacerated wound at the back of the neck. The cause of death was given as cardio-pulmonary arrest due to transection of the spinal cord at the atlanto-occipital joint. On 23 November 2001 the accused were apprehended. One accused gave a confessional statement, after which an axe, a sword and a knife were recovered from bushes in a field. Several eyewitnesses described the sequence of the assault, the weapons used and the role of each accused. Among them, several said one accused struck the victim's head with a stone. Recovered objects were sent for forensic examination.
physical_harm: Death of the victim on the spot; 12 injuries including 10 sharp-weapon wounds, partial amputation of three fingers of left hand and a deep lacerated wound at back of neck with transection of spinal cord
number_of_offences: 1 charged (s.302 r/w s.34 IPC); 1 finally upheld for A-1, A-2 and A-4; A-3's conviction altered to s.304 Part II
motive: alleged: political animosity between the two groups arising from the Gram Panchayat election result
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony (especially PW-6, plus PWs 1, 3, 4, 7, 8) accepted for A-1, A-2 and A-4; post-mortem findings relied on, including the fatal neck injury caused by axe; for A-3, the consistent eyewitness account that he struck the head with a stone
witness_credibility: Trial court and High Court found PW-6 credible and consistent; Supreme Court accepted eyewitness accounts as correctly appreciated for A-1, A-2, A-4; for A-3 the Supreme Court relied on the consistent account of the stone blow, while noting his threats as described by some witnesses
post_offence_conduct: Apprehended on 23.11.2001 and produced before the Circle Inspector; no absconding or flight noted
trial_duration: offence: 15.11.2001; trial judgment: 24.02.2005; High Court: 26.04.2022 (earlier High Court acquittal 21.06.2007, set aside and remanded); Supreme Court: 06.02.2024
legal_representation: Appellants (accused): Gaurav Agrawal, D. Abhinav Rao, Ms. Prerna Robin, Rahul Jajoo, Devadipta Das. State: Krishan Kumar Singh (learned counsel for the State). Respondent No. 2: Sirajudeen, Senior Advocate
investigation_status: FIR registered on complaint of the victim's son; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed 09.01.2002; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: Trial and High Court did not separately analyse A-3's role and mechanically inferred common intention from his presence and family relation with the other accused
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302/34, life imprisonment. High Court (first): acquitted all accused (21.06.2007), set aside by Supreme Court and remanded. High Court (after remand, 26.04.2022): confirmed conviction and dismissed appeals. Supreme Court: convictions of A-1, A-2, A-4 upheld; A-3 convicted under s.304 Part II and sentenced to 10 years
legal_principle_applied: Common intention under s.34 must be shown by evidence; presence and family relation are insufficient. Where common intention to murder is absent, liability may rest on knowledge that the act is likely to cause death, under s.304 Part II
precedent_relied_upon: Camilo Vaz v. State of Goa, (2000) 9 SCC 1; Bawa Singh v. State of Punjab, 1993 Supp (2) SCC 754; Sarup Singh v. State of Haryana, (2009) 16 SCC 479; Ghana Pradhan & Ors. v. State of Orissa, 1991 Supp (2) SCC 451
sentencing_rationale: For A-3: no common intention to murder, no axe used, only a stone; knowledge that a stone blow to the head is likely to cause death; sentence of 10 years under s.304 Part II. For A-1, A-2, A-4: life imprisonment upheld under s.302/34
judicial_mitigating_factors: For A-3: did not wield the axe, had only a stone, merely threatened some witnesses, was not shown to have shared common intention to murder
judicial_aggravating_factors: Fatal injury at the neck inflicted with an axe by A-1, followed by assault by A-2 and A-4; multiple weapons used against the victim
